En todos esos casos, la proposición de ley pactada por PSC y Comuns permite edificar de forma inmediata siempre que sea VPO, sin esperar a que se permita un cambio de uso. A cambio, la ley blinda el uso residencial permanente de todos los pisos de nueva construcción, que solo podrán destinarse a vivienda habitual, para un familiar, segunda residencia o al alquiler dentro de los topes fijados por el Ejecutivo catalán. En ningún caso se permitirán más licencias para construir apartamentos turísticos o alquiler de temporada. Fuentes del Ejecutivo y de los Comuns aseguran que sí se permitirá construir segundas residencias, pero el sector cree que la actual redacción da a entender lo contrario. “No queda claro, dice que el uso debe ser ‘habitual y permanente’. Y eso desvirtúa una proposición que tiene varios puntos que están muy bien”, lamenta Vilajoana, que sí está de acuerdo con las medidas que facilitan construir VPO sin cambiar el planeamiento municipal.

Aplicación en zonas de alta demanda

En principio, la medida se aplicará en los 271 municipios de mercado tensionado, donde reside el 90% de la población. También a las 161 localidades que la normativa catalana establece como áreas de demanda “fuerte y acreditada”, que en muchos casos se solapa con los municipios anteriores. La razón de incluir ambas referencias es la posibilidad de que en algún momento pueda prosperar la ley del Suelo presentada por el PP y respaldada por Vox y Junts, que contempla derogar las zonas tensionadas para acabar de golpe con medidas como el tope a los alquileres. El plan, además, pasará una revisión cada dos años para comprobar si está dando resultados o hace falta modular alguna de las medidas contempladas.

La medida, que tendrá una vigencia de cuatro años prorrogables a otros cuatro, podrá ejecutarse cuando entre en vigor sin tener que pasar por los Ayuntamientos. Es decir, si los consistorios no dicen nada el promotor tendrá preconcedido el aumento de la edificabilidad o el cambio de uso. Sin embargo, los dos grupos entienden que las medidas implican, en cierta medida, una densificación de los municipios y cambios de uso que tal vez los ayuntamientos no deseen para, por ejemplo, preservar el comercio local. Los consistorios podrán rechazar estas medidas mediante un acuerdo plenario en el que acrediten que ya tienen suficiente casas habituales y asequibles para garantizar el derecho al acceso a una vivienda.

World.title: Guardiola rechaza la oferta para ser el técnico de la selección de Italia
World.content:
Pep Guardiola ha rechazado la propuesta de la federación italiana de fútbol para ser el próximo entrenador de su selección, según avanzaron este viernes por la mañana los principales medios italianos y confirmó también EL PAÍS. Horas después, por la tarde, la prensa italiana ha confirmado también que la elección ha recaído finalmente en Andrea Pirlo, exjugador de Milan y Juventus y vencedor del Mundial con Italia en 2006. Como entrenador, ha pasado desde 2020 por Juventus, el turco Fatih Karagumruk y Sampdoria. Ahora es el técnico del United FC, de Dubái, pero se desvinculará del contrato para firmar como técnico de Italia por 1,5 millones por cuatro años, según varios medios.

La decisión ha sido rápida tras la negativa de Guardiola, porque era el plan B. El hasta ahora entrenador del Manchester City se lo había pensado más de cinco días, después de que Paolo Maldini, nuevo director técnico de la federación del calcio y su asesor, Leonardo, viajaran a Barcelona el pasado fin de semana para hacerle la oferta. Lo hicieron a pesar de que el técnico había anunciado, tras dejar el City, que abandonaba temporalmente el fútbol para descansar y estar con su familia. Guardiola no dijo que no de entrada, tentado por su amor a Italia y por la oportunidad de dirigir una de las mejores selecciones de la historia, pero al final ha declinado la invitación.

El técnico catalán se ha declarado honrado por la oferta, pero ha dicho que en este momento prefería no aceptarla. Según fuentes próximas al entrenador, este consideró y evaluó la posibilidad de hacerse cargo de la Azzurra, pero el momento en que llega esta posibilidad no le encaja por cuestiones personales y familiares, al tiempo que sigue vinculado al grupo City para ejercer como asesor de las escuelas de captación.

Guardiola había dejado el club británico con un anuncio muy serio de que quería tomarse una temporada sabática y estar con los suyos: “No hay planes para entrenar por un tiempo. De lo contrario, estaría aquí. Necesito dar un paso atrás”, dijo en mayo.

Sin embargo, ha llegado a reflexionar sobre la oferta italiana, que implicaba libertad total para un gran proyecto a largo plazo para refundar todo el sistema del calcio de arriba a abajo. También un esfuerzo económico de la federación para pagarle. Según La Gazzetta dello Sport el técnico habría pedido 20 millones al año, una cifra no confirmada y que sin embargo nunca se barajó en ninguna de las dos partes. No obstante, Paolo Maldini dijo el jueves que el dinero no era un problema ni la cuestión principal para que Guardiola se decidiera. Vino a decir que era más un dilema personal y de corazón.

El reto para el exbarcelonista era devolver a Italia a la primera fila del fútbol internacional. Es cuatro veces campeona del mundo pero se ha perdido ya los tres últimos mundiales y ha tenido siete técnicos desde 2014.

La confirmación oficial de la propuesta llegó el martes, cuando el presidente de la federación italiana, Giovanni Malagò, admitió que fichar a Guardiola exigiría un fuerte desembolso en las maltrechas arcas de la federación, pero dio a entender que se haría un esfuerzo: “Se han hecho excepciones, excepciones que pueden hacerse con el nombre que en estos momentos suena tanto, Pep Guardiola”, señaló. “No está claro que esto vaya a salir, pero creo que ha sido justo e importante abrir un diálogo y mantenerlo vivo”, reveló. Este jueves Malagò reveló que también ha tanteado a Carlo Ancelotti, actual entrenador de Brasil, que no ha hecho un gran papel en el último mundial.

La opción de Andrea Pirlo, amigo y excompañero de Maldini, y con su misma filosofía del fútbol, era la que tenía más posibilidades, y ha sido finalmente la elegida. Las otras eran Antonio Conte y Roberto Mancini. Conte ya guió la nazionale entre 2014 y 2016 y acaba de dejar el Nápoles tras ganar un scudetto la temporada anterior. Era el candidato preferido de clubes y afición, pero no contaba con el favor de Maldini y su equipo. En cuanto a Mancini, ya dirigió Italia entre 2018 y 2023 y ganó la Eurocopa, pero se marchó repentinamente de mala manera porque prefirió ser entrenador de Arabia Saudí con un sueldo estratosférico (100 millones en cuatro años, aunque fue despedido al cabo de un año), y la polémica no se ha olvidado. El jueves reconoció que la federación no le ha contactado.

World.title: La M.O.D.A.: héroes de Burgos que reivindican a ‘los nadie’ de la vida
World.content:
Una pandilla de amigos montaron una banda en 2010 y hoy es la más importante en la historia de la ciudad y una de las más grandes del panorama español. Los chicos de la Maravillosa Orquesta del Alcohol son profetas en su tierra

Primera mañana de verano en Burgos, con un sol intenso en el cielo azul y las margaritas felices en el campo, cuando se monta la marabunta en la puerta del Cernégula. Se bajan hasta los auxiliares de la ambulancia de Protección Civil. “¡Sois unos artistas!”, exclama un anciano llamado Paco en la puerta de la antigua fonda de la carretera de Arcos, abierta durante 70 años en el actual barrio de San Felices y de la que queda hoy solo el estanco, lugar de peregrinaje de los chicos de la Maravillosa Orquesta del Alcohol (M.O.D.A.) para pillar bocadillos, bebidas y tabaco cuando se escapan de su estudio de grabación a tan solo 200 metros ladera bajo en el parque del Hangar. “Estáis en casa. Venga, pa’ dentro, coged botellas de agua que hace mucho calor”, pide a todos Rosa Melgosa, dueña del Cernégula y citada en la canción de la M.O.D.A. ‘San Felices’: “Y sé que ya hemos vuelto a casa al ver a Rosa en el Cernégula”. Esa casa está ahora repleta de personas que han visto llegar a los miembros de la banda más importante de la ciudad y se han ido directos a por ellos. Algunos estaban en el estanco, otros han salido de un bar cercano, otras han cruzado desde la otra acera, uno se ha bajado de la moto y otros dos de la ambulancia, resuelta la urgencia, se han arrimado también. Incluso un grupo de niños con autismo que sale con sus tutoras “muy fans” del colegio Sagrado Corazón Hermanas Salesianas, justo enfrente del Cernégula, se ha parado para fotografiarse con ellos. Fotos, autógrafos, besos, abrazos y palabras de cariño por todas partes: “sois los mejores”, “gracias por todo”, “no dejéis de tocar”, “Burgos os quiere”… Los seis integrantes de la M.O.D.A. atienden a todos, uno por uno. “Todo esto se monta por las camisetas de tirantes”, asegura David Ruiz, cantante y compositor del grupo. “Si no las llevamos puestas, la gente no nos reconoce. Cuando vamos vestidos de paisanos normales, pasamos desapercibidos en todo Burgos como si fuéramos Clark Kent”, añade. “Al ponernos estas camisetas, es como si fueran el traje y la capa de Superman”, dice el baterista Caleb Melguizo con media sonrisa. “O Superlópez, que nos pega más”, añade Ruiz.

Bien sean Superman o Superlópez, las camisetas de tirantes son un elemento de distinción, pero, lejos de cualquier heroísmo de superioridad, es una declaración de intenciones. “Es una prenda que puede llevar cualquiera. Desde nuestros abuelos hasta un currante”, explica Ruiz. De hecho, el grupo tiene una canción llamada precisamente ‘Héroes del sábado’, todo un himno entre sus seguidores coreado a pleno pulmón en sus multitudinarios conciertos, sobre todo, en el verso: “No te olvides de dónde vienes”. Ellos, burgaleses todos menos el guitarrista y productor Nacho Mur, “aunque ya está adoptado”, no se olvidan de dónde vienen. La ciudad de Burgos, con su bella catedral presidiendo la silueta desde cualquier horizonte, es su casa, como lo podría ser también la provincia repleta de pueblos de la que vienen algunos de ellos y sus familias, toda esa tierra a la que cantan y que reivindican por la población llana, por la gente anónima formada por “los nadie”, tal y como dice, parafraseando al escritor uruguayo Eduardo Galeano, Ruiz, quien lleva un tatuaje de Johnny Cash en el brazo en honor “al cantante de los desfavorecidos”. Así lo han hecho desde que nació la M.O.D.A. en 2010, después de que David Ruiz decidió crear una banda con sus amigos de los parques a su vuelta de tocar por los bares de Dublín, y lo siguen haciendo hoy con su último disco, San Felices (Universal), un homenaje al barrio donde tienen su local de ensayo y oficina.

Un detalle de las guitarras de La M.O.D.A. en su local de ensayo, en Burgos. Jacobo Medrano

Cuando asentaron su centro de operaciones en este barrio en 2011, todo era campo. Los miembros de la M.O.D.A. fueron de sus primeros pobladores. San Felices se levantó en la antigua barriada de los ferroviarios y, por eso, al pasear entre sus amplias calles de edificios residenciales nuevos, se ven, a modo decorativo con sus hierbajos, las viejas vías de tren. El local de ensayo y la oficina descansan en El Hangar, que fue una estación y que hoy alberga además un centro cultural y una sala de conciertos dentro de un parque con un antiguo vagón de mercancías. “En Burgos, se dice que antes había solo dos estaciones: el invierno y la de la Renfe”, cuenta el saxofonista Alvar de Pablo. Eso era cuando no había cambio climático ni tampoco existía la M.O.D.A., una banda que se puede decir que, tras su éxito de público en toda España, se ha convertido en la más importante en la historia de Burgos. Hay hechos que lo confirman: el año pasado, tocaron en una noche memorable ante 50.000 personas en las Fiestas de San Pedro y San Pablo de Burgos; y este año, son cabeza de cartel del festival Sonorama Ribera donde volverán a tocar ante cerca 30.000 personas en Aranda de Duero. Ese día festivalero, compartirán escenario principal con Leiva, otro cabeza de cartel que colabora en el disco San Felices, en la canción ‘Subiendo como El Chava Jiménez’.

Este lunes por la mañana acaban de llegar, precisamente, las cajas con las nuevas camisetas del merchandising inspirada en la canción dedicada al ciclista Chava Jiménez. Tiene un aire muy noventero. La oficina de la M.O.D.A. está en la planta de arriba de la sala Hangar por lo que huele todavía a la fiesta del fin de semana de los conciertos. En los pasillos para llegar al local de ensayo, se ven carteles de The Cure o Jimi Hendrix. Choli, el dueño del Hangar, aparece y da abrazos a todos. “A ver si quedamos para hacer una comida antes de las vacaciones”, dice. Hasta este álbum en el que ficharon por la major Universal, el grupo se editaba sus discos y controlaba todo: contratación, merchandising, comunicación, redes sociales… “Nosotros siempre hemos ido arando todo con la mano, pero ya veíamos que nos pasaban con la cosechadora a toda hostia”, explica el acordeonista José Ángel Hortigüela, Joselito, en referencia a otros grupos que trabajan desde hace años con grandes discográficas. “Queríamos probarlo para poder dejar de dedicar tantas horas a lo extramusical”, añade Ruiz.

Regalos personalizados de los fans de la banda. Jacobo Medrano

Más allá de este fichaje, la esencia de la M.O.D.A. es la misma desde que en 2010 dieron su primer concierto para colegas en Estudio 27, un bar que ya no existe que estaba ubicado en los bajos del plantío. La esencia de una pandilla de amigos que representa la llaneza de la gente común burgalesa. Nacho Mur, que también toca la mandolina, llegó el último desde Madrid en 2017 y pronto pudo comprobarlo. “El día que me incorporé oficialmente al grupo pensé que las camisetas de tirantes blancas venían dadas por contrato o algo así. Fue una equivocación. Aquí cada uno se compra las suyas y se encarga de ellas”, recuerda con una sonrisa. Eso ha llevado a que alguna vez hayan tenido que ir a por otras de urgencia porque alguno se la dejó en casa o, en un despiste, alguno pilló una de color gris y eso no se permite. También los ha llevado a rechazar “una buena pasta” por tenerlas bajo patrocinio. La independencia de la banda sigue intacta como el primer día. “No hacemos nada con instituciones ni queremos ser usados en política”, explica Ruiz. “Hace unos años nos ofrecieron 50.000 euros para un apoyo institucional y dijimos que no. Entonces, era un dineral que nos ayudaba a mucho, pero ya tomamos esa decisión y seguimos con ella a rajatabla”. En los últimos años, encima, han tenido que hacer frente al impago de la plataforma de venta de entradas Wegow, que entró en concurso de acreedores y dejó a muchos artistas sin su dinero. La M.O.D.A. fue la banda más afectada con decenas de miles de euros perdidos. “Hemos decidido centrarnos en lo que nos llevó un día a meternos en un garaje, que son las canciones, los conciertos y el público”, dice Ruiz. Ellos, aparte de demandar colectivamente a la plataforma, siguen currando.

La banda pasea al lado de la catedral de Burgos. Jacobo Medrano

El pueblo de Burgos se lo reconoce, y no sólo porque acude a sus conciertos con pasión desmedida. En este lunes, para la sesión de fotos, deciden ir con sus camisetas de tirantes blancas al centro de la ciudad y reciben oleadas de cariño y admiración. Obreros que desde lo alto de las grúas les saludan a gritos, señoras que sentadas en bancos de los parques les llaman “guapos” y “bonitos”, jóvenes que desde las ventanas de sus pisos les corean o viandantes que piden selfies, estrechan las manos o les recuerdan aquella actuación que los emocionó. Cuando paran a comprar en la pastelería Dieste unas roscas de Medina y unos chevaliers, famosos dulces burgaleses, la dependienta obliga a salir a los maestros pasteleros para saludarles. Y, cuando llegan a la estación de autobuses para las fotografías de este reportaje, se monta el follón. La gente se amontona para hacerse una foto. Una de ellas es Marta Hebrero, la jefa de la estación. “La canción ‘Héroes de sábado’ es el himno de mi hija Ángela y el mío”, confiesa emocionada. “¡Os queremos ya en el Sonorama!”, exclama Carmen García, una “señora mayor” amante del grupo y vecina de Aranda de Duero. “En la provincia de Burgos, estos chicos son tan buenos como el vino”, añade.

Uno de los éxitos de la M.O.D.A. es su capacidad para ser un grupo intergeneracional. Se comprueba en los paseos por Burgos, donde lo mismo gusta a adolescentes que a ancianos. Incluso a niños, como India, de 10 años, y Pedro, de 8, que están en la estación con su madre Alejandra y ya cuentan que los han visto en directo. “Ver en nuestros conciertos a abuelos, padres, hijos y nietos es lo más lo más bonito que nos viene pasando desde hace unos años”, asegura el saxofonista Alvar de Pablo. Sin formar parte del indie ni de ninguna M.O.D.A. musical, la banda tiene esa rara cualidad del rock urbano, como Extremoduro o Rosendo, que llega a varias generaciones por su afán a ser coreado. Hay en sus canciones, impregnadas de un aroma a folk irlandés y cantadas con la particularísima voz ronca de David Ruiz, una sensación de pertenencia. “Para nosotros, siempre ha sido más interesante estar fuera del indie, aunque, en principio, eso nos perjudicaba en el circuito de la música en directo en España. Es mejor que no te acaben de encajar en ningún sitio porque si no ya estás encasillado en una cosa y te limita mucho”, afirma el cantante.

Una canción del último disco candidata a convertirse en otro himno es ‘Alsa pa Madrid’, en homenaje a todos esos jóvenes que antes y ahora han tenido que dejar Burgos o sus localidades de Castilla y León para buscarse la vida en la gran ciudad. Solo en Burgos hay más pueblos que en todo Portugal. Es la provincia con más pueblos en toda Europa con un total de 371. Y ‘Alsa pa Madrid’, como tantas canciones de la M.O.D.A., atraviesan esa realidad. La propia jefa de la estación de autobuses cuenta que los vio en Villadiego, un pueblecito de la provincia, dentro de una de las cuatro giras que desde 2018 han hecho gratis por los pueblos despoblados de Burgos. “No cabía nadie en el pueblo. Estaba todo a reventar. Y todos felices”, recuerda la mujer. “Para nosotros, es genial hacer estas giras”, explica el bajista Jorge Juan Mariscal. “Viene gente desde a tomar por culo y se vuelcan. Los más ancianos te dicen que no habían visto el pueblo así de gente desde hacía 60 años”, añade.

Los miembros del grupo en un autobús Alsa, en la estación de Burgos. Jacobo Medrano

El grupo al completo abandona Burgos. Primero a través de la N-I y, luego, por carreteras secundarias, su furgoneta se adentra por bellos parajes camino de Sedano, lugar de descanso y veraneo de Miguel Delibes, quien conoció a su esposa en este coqueto territorio conquistado por la piedra en su arquitectura. Años atrás, allí tocaron en su gira de apoyo a los sitios despoblados y conocieron a Florentín, un anciano, ya fallecido, que les recibía con una olla de comida cada vez que iban y les dejó el amplio balcón de su casa cuando tuvieron que improvisar y no pudieron tocar en la plaza ante el riesgo de lluvias. “Estaba todo lleno de gente. Ahí, pusimos el tenderete de los bocadillos y no se podía ni pasar a por uno”, rememora Alberto Peña, un hombre de 70 años amigo de Florentín. Peña cuenta que también conoció a Delibes, quien se quedaba a dormir encima de la antigua fonda y, ya después, se compró una casa con su mujer para veranear y “montar en bici” todos los años. Su nieta Rosa sale de casa y se aviva al ver a los seis integrantes de la M.O.D.A. al completo. Pide una foto y que le firmen la camiseta blanca que lleva puesta. “Artistas, que sois unos artistas. Estáis en casa, por favor, pasad a tomar un agua fresca”, dice el abuelo. Ellos obedecen.

Parte de la gran conexión del grupo con la gente de Burgos, vino después de la publicación en 2021 del disco Nuevo cancionero burgalés, con el apoyo del grupo folclórico burgalés Fetén Fetén. En esa obra, que transpiraba amor por la tierra burgalesa al recuperar el cancionero popular de principios del siglo XX de Federico Olmeda y Antonio José, tocaron una tecla importante para ellos y su público. “Flipamos porque nadie nos había hablado de ellos nunca en el colegio, ni institucionalmente. O tenías la suerte de que en tu casa los conocían o no teníamos ni idea. Son canciones que podían haber sido escritas ahora con letras guapísimas”, afirma Ruiz. “Comunican algo muy importante y no solo en Burgos, sino en Andalucía o incluso en México. Ellos ponen el nombre de su pueblo o de su ciudad en unas letras que vinculan con sus abuelos”, añade el baterista Caleb Melguizo.

Los miembros de La M.O.D.A. pasean por el páramo del pueblo Quintanaloma, en Burgos. Jacobo Medrano

La furgoneta se detiene en Quintanaloma, el pueblo con solo un habitante en invierno en el que nacieron los padres del acordeonista Joselito y en donde el grupo tiene una especie de almacén con las cosas y regalos que no les entran en la oficina de Burgos. Tras atravesar una serpenteante carretera por la que se cruzan ciervos y hay que adelantar a un tractor, aparece en lo alto de la loma un pueblecito que rebosa encanto con la emblemática Casa Torre, testigo silente de siglos de historia. El atardecer del verano recién estrenado hace relucir a los campos amarillos en un color dorado. Un coche se detiene a llegar al camino en el que se está haciendo la sesión de fotos. La pareja de ancianos parece que se baja del coche a quejarse. “¡Oye, chicos!”, grita el hombre. “¿Os podemos tirar unas fotos?”. Han reconocido a los miembros de la M.O.D.A.. “Por sus camisetas, cómo si no”, dice la mujer al ser preguntada.

De vuelta a Burgos, el grupo cuenta que en el próximo otoño van a hacer otra gira por pueblos vacíos. En el mismo formato: gratis, con los instrumentos justos y “ganando humanamente muchísimo”. En otoño, también volverán a tocar en el Movistar Arena ante 17.500 personas. Será la quinta vez que lo llenan desde que lo hicieron por primera vez en 2018. “Venimos del barro. No se nos olvida. Somos unos currantes”, asegura Ruiz. “Para nosotros, un héroe es el que se lo curra mucho, crea con poco y ha tirado para adelante con todo. Nosotros venimos de héroes. Porque nuestros padres y nuestros abuelos no se podían prácticamente plantear el dedicarse a la música, pero, gracias a su sacrificio, nosotros nos hemos podido dedicar a ello”, reflexiona.

Los miembros de La M.O.D.A. posan en las afueras de Quintanaloma, en Burgos. Jacobo Medrano

Al cerrar sus conciertos convertidos en fiestas de coros y bailes, tocan ‘Héroes del sábado’ y ‘Mañana voy a Burgos’. Ataviados con sus camisetas de tirantes blancas, los seis miembros de la M.O.D.A. se desgañitan en el colofón final. Ellos insisten siempre que esas camisetas dan superpoderes. Quizá porque, entre risas y algo de vergüenza, cuentan el día que la policía detuvo a algunos de ellos en Burgos cuando en 2020, en plena pandemia, se les ocurrió la brillante idea de salir a pegar carteles con la publicidad que habían hecho de una nueva canción y, al entretenerse para ponerlos todos, quedaron en la calle fuera del toque de queda y los agentes les pillaron. Se los llevaron a comisaría. Allí, a la espera de ser atendidos por el comisario, un agente preguntó: “¿Vosotros no sois los de la M.O.D.A.?”. Al afirmar con la cabeza, se armó la marabunta y el agente dijo: “¿Qué hacéis poniendo los carteles vosotros? ¿No tenéis a nadie que os haga estas cosas?”. Entonces, informado ya de todo, apareció el comisario y, al verlos vestidos de paisano, dijo con las manos en la cabeza: “Me pincho y no sangro”. Habían detenido a los de la M.O.D.A. Así que empezaron a pedir autógrafos y hacerse fotos con aquellos héroes de Burgos, sólo que vestidos de Clark Kent.

World.title: Europa observa la IA desde la barrera
World.content:
Artículos estrictamente de opinión que responden al estilo propio del autor. Estos textos de opinión han de basarse en datos verificados y ser respetuosos con las personas aunque se critiquen sus actos. Todas las tribunas de opinión de personas ajenas a la Redacción de EL PAÍS llevarán, tras la última línea, un pie de autor —por conocido que éste sea— donde se indique el cargo, título, militancia política (en su caso) u ocupación principal, o la que esté o estuvo relacionada con el tema abordado

La rivalidad tecnológica entre Estados Unidos y China suele describirse como una guerra de chips, pero la etiqueta se queda corta. La verdadera pugna abarca todo el ecosistema de la inteligencia artificial: el hardware que ejecuta los modelos, el software que lo hace utilizable y el diseño de los propios modelos. En los dos primeros frentes la competencia se ha reducido a dos empresas, Nvidia y Huawei. Europa, pese a tener un papel imprescindible en las máquinas que fabrican los chips, mira la pugna desde fuera.

En hardware, EE UU sigue a la cabeza. Nvidia controla cerca de la mitad de los chips de IA instalados del mundo y hasta dos tercios de la capacidad de cálculo. Huawei es su rival más serio, pero sus procesadores Ascend aún se quedan atrás en memoria, herramientas para programadores y eficiencia: para igualar el rendimiento consumen entre dos y cuatro veces más energía.

La brecha importa menos de lo que parece. Los controles que impone Washington a las exportaciones de los chips más avanzados, más los subsidios de Pekín a sus empresas, junto a las compras preferentes y la energía barata para quien usa Ascend, han creado un mercado cautivo capaz de sostener a Huawei y reinvertir esos ingresos en investigación. De esta forma, China gana tiempo: presiona a Washington para conseguir los microprocesadores más avanzados mientras impulsa una alternativa propia, una doble vía que el enfoque transaccional estadounidense ha facilitado en lugar de cerrar.

Lo que hace duradera la ventaja de Nvidia no es la fabricación de chips avanzados, sino haber construido durante años un ecosistema de software —CUDA— que se ha convertido en el estándar del sector. Como casi todo el hardware instalado es de Nvidia, los programadores trabajan sobre CUDA; eso agranda su comunidad y su biblioteca de código y hace cada vez más difícil migrar a un rival. El resultado son márgenes de negocio del 70% al 80%.

La respuesta de Huawei sigue el manual del sector: subvencionar la adopción y llevar a los programadores chinos al software del país. En agosto de 2025 abrió el código de piezas clave de su herramienta CANN —un golpe directo al modelo cerrado de CUDA— y atrajo a laboratorios y universidades chinas. Los programadores aún se quejan de fallos en CANN y de que los 20 años de ventaja de CUDA no tienen rival; pero hace dos años nada de esto existía.

El lanzamiento de Kimi K3 este mes de julio mostró la velocidad a la que surgen nuevos modelos de IA cada vez más competitivos. El modelo de Moonshot AI, con 2,8 billones de parámetros, es el mayor publicado nunca en abierto —libre para usar y adaptar—, solo por detrás de Claude Fable 5 y GPT-5.6 en las pruebas de la empresa. La aparición de Kimi K3 preocupó a los inversores y provocó una caída del 1,4% del Nasdaq, así como fuertes descensos en las empresas de semiconductores. El presidente chino, Xi Jinping, usó la reciente Conferencia Mundial de IA de Shanghái para alinear a Pekín con el código abierto: publicarlo así es ya política de Estado. Y Moonshot fijó K3 en un rango de precio de gama alta, no de saldo: los laboratorios chinos han dejado de vender barato.

K3 también deja ver lo que China aún no ha resuelto. Los datos de Moonshot apuntan a que Kimi K3 fue entrenado con chips de exportación de Nvidia, no con los Ascend de Huawei. Y DeepSeek, según se informa, también volvió a utilizar Nvidia después de una prueba con Ascend, reservando este para el servicio diario. Es decir, Nvidia mantiene una ventaja decisiva en el entrenamiento de modelos gracias a CUDA, un terreno en el que Huawei aún no ha logrado imponerse.

Europa, mientras, sigue en mala posición. La holandesa ASML mantiene el monopolio en las máquinas de litografía más avanzadas, el centro belga IMEC es líder en investigación, al tiempo que desarrolla una ciencia de IA de primer nivel. Pero le faltan diseñadores de chips de IA de talla mundial y un modelo de programación como CUDA o CANN. Como hardware y software se diseñan juntos, no tener uno hace casi imposible el otro. Es un proveedor imprescindible en una carrera en la que no compite: el valor va a quien controla el diseño del chip y el software, no a quien vende las piezas. Su peso, además, es menor de lo que se creía: cuando Pekín pidió concesiones en 2025, reclamó memoria de alta velocidad, no máquinas de litografía.

¿Qué puede hacer? Primero, aprender de China en vez de despreciarla. Partió de la dependencia y recorta distancia con diplomacia, demanda cautiva, subvenciones y modelos abiertos. Segundo, aprender de Airbus, que funcionó porque el reparto de tareas respondía a ventajas reales y puso la lógica comercial por encima de la política. La analogía cojea —la aviación no dependía de un proveedor de software—, y por eso esa disciplina importa más, no menos. Europa tiene elementos para luchar por un hueco en esta carrera: ASML, IMEC, Infineon, STMicroelectronics, Zeiss... Tercero, impulsar la demanda. EuroHPC, las fábricas de IA e InvestAI financian la oferta de semiconductores, pero no la demanda, y las compras públicas siguen siendo competencia de cada Estado. Administración pública, sanidad, defensa e investigación son los ámbitos por donde empezar.

Nada de esto garantiza el desarrollo próximo de una Nvidia europea; Airbus tardó 20 años en convertirse en un competidor sólido. Pero la alternativa es un futuro en el que la infraestructura de cálculo europea, y las condiciones en que sus empresas crean modelos de IA, queden subordinadas para siempre a Washington o a Pekín. La competencia ya no es quién diseña el mejor chip, sino quién controla la infraestructura entera, hoy de tres capas, no dos. Europa debería, al menos, intentarlo en serio.

World.title: Blood on Her Tongue: A modern vampire tale not for the squeamish
World.content:
Johanna van Veen’s gothic horror Blood on Her Tongue offers up a classic vampire tale with some modern contemplations.

The book follows Lucy Goedhart as she is called to the ominously named Zwartwater (black water) estate, where her sister has taken ill. In 1887, there isn’t much in the way of medical treatment, but Lucy’s sister Sarah isn’t fighting off a regular illness.

Sarah has become obsessed with a body found in the bog of the vast estate and since interacting with the 300-year-old corpse she has become increasingly incoherent, struggles with taking care of herself and has developed an insatiable hunger.

As Lucy tries desperately to save her sister, she finds that her sister’s husband, her sister’s doctor and childhood friend, and several other characters who are present at the remote manor house all have their own interests and motivations – some as dangerous as whatever condition is plaguing Sarah.

The book is not for those easily bothered by gore. The title – Blood on Her Tongue – is a pretty good indication of what is to come. Van Veen does not shy away from the horror elements, including two separate scenes of eyeball gouging.

Like any good horror novel, the macabre monster is not the scariest part. The threats Lucy faces are from the men surrounding her sister. Her brother-in-law attempts to seduce Lucy while badgering her to send Sarah away to an asylum.

Sarah’s doctor expresses his own interest in Lucy, pushing his vision of the future while supposedly devoting himself to his patient. The mores of 19th-century upper-class society may be the biggest piece of villainy of all.

In the tradition of Dracula, Blood on Her Tongue tells its story through letters, journal entries and newspaper clippings. The personal correspondence adds to the claustrophobia of the work, with everyone limited to an isolated house, but the media reports remind the reader that the world outside does exist.

The work is the second book from Dutch author Johanna van Veen. It was published in 2025 in English and became a USA Today bestseller. Her first book, My Darling Dreadful Thing, was nominated for the Bram Stoker Award for best horror novel. Van Veen grew up in the Netherlands as a triplet, something that influenced her writing about the sisters Lucy and Sarah.

If horror is your thing, Blood on Her Tongue will creep you out and keep you turning the pages.

You can get your copy at the American Book Center.

World.title: Thousands cross finishing line as Nijmegen Vierdaagse ends
World.content:
The 108th edition of the Nijmegense Vierdaagse (four-day march) ended on Friday, with tens of thousands of walkers being welcomed with flowers by well-wishers.

British walker Simon Brownlee crossed the finishing line ahead of the rest of the walkers for the 27th time, local media reported. Brownlee, who completed the distance before 10am, told local broadcaster Omroep Gelderland that the walk “felt like home”. “I’m happy it is over and I can now relax,” he said.

Wheelchair participant Ronald van Dort was the very first person to finish, picking up his seventh medal for completing the event.

Over 45,000 walkers from 70 countries took part in this year’s series, which is proving increasingly popular among the young. Ten years ago, 7.5% of the walkers were aged 21 to 30, but this year their number rose to over 20%.

This year the event was marred by a fatal shooting just outside the area where the Vierdaagsefeesten, the street festivities accompanying the annual four-day marches, were taking place. One man has been arrested.

The shooting, and other crowd problems, led the organisers to cancel performances by urban scene artists such as Ronnie Flex and Lil’ Kleine because their presence was “attracting the wrong sort of people”, the AD reported.

World.title: Dozens of women forced into prostitution by Romanian gang
World.content:
Dozens of women may have been forced into working as prostitutes in Amsterdam’s red light district by a Romanian gang, Dutch police confirmed on Friday.

The statement follows a joint Dutch and Romanian campaign against human trafficking in the area earlier this month. Seven men were arrested during a string of raids on July 14 – four in the Netherlands and three in Romania. All were Romanian nationals.

Shortly after the arrests, police issued a video interview with one of the victims speaking Romanian, which has led more women to come forward and has resulted in other information reaching the police, the statement said.

Police now say they have spoken to several victims and say they believe more women have been trafficked. They too are said to be Romanian.

The women were lured to Amsterdam with the promise of high earnings but found themselves forced into working in brothels and handing over their earnings to the gang. They were also forced to pay “rent” for their rooms.

None of the men had jobs but were big spenders, buying expensive clothes and cars and gambling heavily, the statement said. The gang also treated part of the red light district as their “personal kingdom”.

Four men remain in custody in the Netherlands, one of whom was extradited from Romania. Another man may also be extradited soon, RTL said. They are all suspected of human trafficking and forming a criminal organisation.

According to the Parool, two of the suspects are half brothers aged 44 and 45 who have earlier convictions for trafficking in women in Romania.

More arrests have not been ruled out.

A year ago, Dutch and Romanian police arrested 13 people in a joint investigation into human trafficking and the forced prostitution of Romanian women, mainly in and around Amsterdam.

World.title: Singer Sophie Straat cleared of discrimination over mosh pit
World.content:
Discrimination hotlines in both the Netherlands and Belgium have concluded that Dutch singer Sophie Straat did not discriminate when she asked “all white men to step back” during two of her recent performances.

Last month at the Best Kept Secret festival in Beekse Bergen, Straat — real name Sophie Schwartz — asked for space for women, queer people and people of colour in the “mosh pit”, an area in front of the stage where fans dance chaotically.

She made the same request on Monday during a performance in Ghent, Belgium.

The Dutch discrimination hotline Discriminatie.nl said it received hundreds of complaints but maintains that Straat’s comments do not amount to discrimination against white men based on their colour or gender.

“The call only concerned one short, one-off mosh pit for these groups,” said the hotline. “Therefore, visitors were not refused entry to the concert.”

Belgian authorities reached the same conclusion after receiving some 200 complaints following her performance in Ghent.

“Although the statement may be perceived as polarizing or offensive, in this context it must be seen as a symbolic and artistic expression,” a spokesperson for the Belgian discrimination hotline Unia told the Flemish broadcaster VRT.

“According to the case law of the European Court of Human Rights, artistic and political expressions enjoy broad protection under freedom of expression, even when they provoke, shock or offend.”

Hate messages and death threats

Straat wrote on Instagram earlier this month that she has received “a wave of sexist, antisemitic hate messages and (death) threats, some more explicit and creative than others”.

She has also questioned where the left-wing media has been in all this, saying the public narrative is being controlled by the right.

The singer, who was raised in a Jewish home in Amsterdam’s de Pijp neighbourhood and is known for her protest songs, has said she never wanted to exclude anyone but rather wanted to make room for people who feel unsafe in a mosh pit.

World.title: Youngster arrested for participating in sadistic online network
World.content:
Police have arrested a young man from Noord Holland who they suspect of being part of the sadistic online Com network “764”.

The public prosecution department reported the arrest on Thursday, saying the suspect encouraged underage girls to cut themselves and write his online name on a wall with their own blood—so-called “bloodsigns”.

He also is said to have prompted them to write his name on their bodies with a marker, known as“fansigns”. Both are practices within the Com movement—short for The Community—for members to gain prestige.

The suspect himself, who was also charged with aggravated assault, exploitation of underage girls and possession of images of sexual child abuse, was a minor at the time of the alleged crimes. Because of that, no further details are being released.

The Com network consists of various chat groups where members recruit vulnerable young people and force them to commit acts including assault, sexual abuse and murder.

The members, from all corners of the globe, then share images of these acts online in private chat groups, using such platforms as Telegram and Discord.

According to NOS, at least 70 Dutch people are involved in this movement known as “nihilistic extremism” because the incitement to commit such extreme violence doesn’t have a clear ideological motive.

The phenomenon is especially attractive to young men.

World.title: Dangerous drivers face extra surveillance under points system
World.content:
The police and justice ministry officials are working on a system which would see traffic offenders being given points for dangerous driving – which will lead to persistent offenders coming under extra surveillance.

Motorists who have collected six points for using a mobile phone while driving or not wearing a seatbelt would come under the tougher regime, RTL Nieuws reported on Friday. No start date has yet been set.

The points will be awarded in addition to regular fines. The number of points will depend on the seriousness of the offences and speeding tickets recorded by camera will not be included.

The new system is being devised in an effort to tackle persistent offenders who do not change their behaviour despite being fined multiple times, RTL said. Last year, almost 30,000 people would have had at least six points if the new system had been in existence.

“Research shows that people who don’t stick to the rules are often responsible for accidents,” Achilles Damen from the public prosecution department told the broadcaster.

The privacy implications of monitoring specific individuals are still being assessed, RTL said.

World.title: Ajax beat Vojvodina in Conference League qualifier, Twente lose
World.content:
Ajax kicked off their European football campaign with a 4-1 win over Serbian club Vojvodina in the second qualification round of the Conference League competition in Novi Sad on Thursday evening.

The simple win sets the Amsterdammers up in a strong position ahead of the return match next week. If Ajax win again, they will meet either Irish side Shelbourne FC or Estonian club Nõmme Kalju in the third qualification round for the third-tier European competition.

The Amsterdam goal total included one for 16-year-old debutant Mohamed Abdalla, who became the youngest player to score for a Dutch club in Europe.

There was disappointment for FC Twente, who are hoping to qualify for the group stage of the Europa League. They lost 1-2 at home to Hungarian side Ferencváros and will have to pull out all the stops during the away leg next week to remain in the competition.

If they do lose, Twente will move down to the qualification rounds of the Conference League.

PSV Eindhoven and Feyenoord have qualified directly for the Champions League while NEC is taking part in the qualification competition. AZ, as winners of the KNVB Cup last season, will take part in the Europa League competition.

World.title: Unilever backs London for food division secondary listing
World.content:
Unilever’s food division, which is being sold to US sauce and spice producer McCormick, will have a secondary listing on the London stock exchange, despite an intensive lobbying campaign to list in Amsterdam.

Unilever itself has been based in London, and listed there, since 2020.

Unilever said in a statement that the secondary listing is separate to McCormick’s plans to establish an international headquarters in the Netherlands and maintain Unilever Food’s R&D facilities and operations in Wageningen.

This “reflects its commitment to the European market and the critical role the Netherlands will continue to play in the combined company”, the statement said.

Economic affairs minister Heleen Herbert said in a reaction to the sale when it was announced in March that the cabinet had already discussed developments with Unilever and would talk to the new owner “such as about a listing on the Amsterdam stock exchange”.

Unilever’s ice cream arm, spun off in 2024, is listed on the Amsterdam stock exchange as the Magnum Ice Cream Company and is headquartered in the Dutch capital.

The sale of the food arm means there is nothing left of the original Dutch part of Unilever, which was set up in 1930 through the merger of the Dutch Margarine Unie and British soap maker Lever Brothers. Unilever now focuses on personal care and household cleaning products.

Keeping dogs and cats chained up at home will be banned in Poland from next year, after President Karol Nawrocki signed into law a bill prohibiting the practice. His decision ends a long-running dispute over the issue, after Nawrocki last year vetoed a previous proposal to ban chaining because it also included what he argued were excessive and unrealistic additional measures on minimum kennel sizes for dogs. Zawetowana w listopadzie 2025 r. ustawa łańcuchowa była źle przygotowana i przeregulowana, ponieważ nakładała na obywateli obowiązki, których wielu nie byłoby w stanie spełnić. Dzisiaj otrzymujemy ustawę lepszą, z pozytywnym głosem takich podmiotów jak rolniczy samorząd.… pic.twitter.com/h7kIAI77KR — Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) July 24, 2026 The new law bans owners from tethering dogs and cats at home. Animals must be kept either inside the house, in a fenced garden or, if that is not possible, in a kennel “large enough for the animal to move freely and satisfy its natural needs”. Dogs kept in kennels must be provided with daily exercise outside of it. Dogs and cats can still be put on leashes in certain situations, such as when they are being walked, but also during transport, while participating in shows, performances or training, if they are at vets or groomers, or if they represent a danger to humans or other animals. Now that the bill has been signed by Nawrocki, it will be published in the official Journal of Laws (Dziennik Ustaw), after which it goes into force 12 months later. The new measures represent a successful second attempt to introduce a leashing ban. A previous bill was approved by parliament last September. However, in December, Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, announced that he was vetoing it. The president argued that, “although the intention – protecting animals – is just and noble, the law itself was poorly drafted”. In particular, he said that elements introducing minimum sizes for dog kennels were unrealistic and would “harm farmers, breeders and ordinary rural households”. After an attempt by parliament to overturn the veto failed, legislators went back to the drawing board and, following discussions with the president’s chancellery and animal rights groups, drafted a compromise bill that was approved by parliament earlier this month. The bill received support from the current ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, as well as most MPs from the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), the main opposition party. The far-right Confederation (Konfederacja) and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) voted against it. Thousands of people have protested in Warsaw against President @NawrockiKn's veto of a law that would have banned the chaining up of dogs Parliament will vote on Wednesday on whether to overturn Nawrocki's veto, which would require a three-fifths majority https://t.co/0GRup2sppb — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 15, 2025 “We now have a better law, with positive feedback from entities such as the agricultural chamber,” said Nawrocki today. “It demonstrates that the pressure of the presidential veto makes sense. My previous decision to refuse to sign this bill forced the government and parliament to work harder.” However, although Nawrocki said the new law would no longer entail “rigid and costly requirements” for kennels, his office noted in a separate statement that the legislation requires the agriculture minister to issue a regulation establishing “minimum kennel area, taking into account the dog’s size”. It remains unclear if and how that would differ from the requirements Nawrocki previously vetoed. The presidential chancellery also noted that the law itself already outlines that kennels must be made of “wood or wood-like material with thermal insulation”, must be insulated from the ground, and must have openings on at least two sides to allow light and air to enter. A dog who throws a ball to passers-by from a balcony above one of Poland’s most famous streets and waits for them to throw it back has become a star. Police officers and rangers have stepped up joint patrols in Poland’s mountainous Tatra National Park during the peak summer season, following a spate of rule-breaking including swimming in the park’s lakes and ponds, driving cars and going off marked trails. Meanwhile, national park authorities have repeated warnings that bathing, littering and breaking other rules can damage the park’s fragile ecosystem. Local police officers have joined Tatra National Park rangers on patrols on popular tourist routes. On one such patrol last week, officers focused on education and prevention, reminding visitors not to leave marked trails or litter and explaining how to behave safely and responsibly in the mountains. They also checked that organised groups were accompanied by qualified mountain guides, as required by law. Fines for such offences range from 50 zloty (€11.55) to as much as 1,000 zloty (€231) in the event of environmental damage or multiple offences. Police said that all visitors encountered during the patrol were complying with the park’s regulations. However, they added that similar patrols would continue on a regular basis. The Tatra National Park, home to Poland’s highest peaks, and the nearby mountain resort of Zakopane are among the country’s most popular holiday destinations, with crowds taking to park trails in the summer season. The park, the most visited of Poland’s 23 national parks, welcomed a record 5.3 million visitors in 2025 and offers 275 km of marked hiking trails, including high-altitude routes that connect at several points with the adjacent national park in Slovakia. 🚨 Ukraiński Influencer wjechał nielegalnie samochodem na Morskie oko 🗣️: Jesteśmy pierwszymi ludźmi w historii, którzy wjechali samochodem nad Morskie Oko. To było jedno z miejsc, do których chcieliśmy dotrzeć podczas tej podróży i wszyscy znajomi oraz przyjaciele mówili, że… pic.twitter.com/tA9shZ6Rqk — Pigułka 💊 (@informacyjnie) May 23, 2026 This season has already seen a number of high-profile cases of transgressions of the park’s strict rules. In May, a Ukrainian social media influencer sparked outrage after driving a sports car along a road closed to traffic to Morskie Oko, a picturesque lake nestled between the mountains. As a result, he was banned from entering Poland and other Schengen Area countries for five years. Tourists have also been filmed entering Morskie Oko and other protected lakes and ponds, which is not permitted in the national park. This month, a group of young Dutch tourists were filmed bathing in Przedni Staw Polski in the Valley of the Five Lakes, one of the Tatras’ best-known hiking destinations. Witnesses repeatedly warned the group that entering the lake was prohibited, but they ignored the warnings, reports Gazeta Wyborcza. Park authorities have responded to such incidents by reminding visitors of the reasons for the strict rules. “Tatra ponds are incredibly delicate ecosystems. Cosmetics, UV filters, insect repellents, and bacteria entering the water can have a long-lasting impact on its chemical composition and the organisms living in the lakes,” they warned. A national park in Poland’s southern mountains has completed testing of an electric bus that could replace horse-drawn carriages carrying tourists to a famous lake. World.title: Polish opposition PiS party set to split, with over 30 MPs being expelled
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. More than 30 MPs from the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s main opposition party, have effectively resigned after refusing to sign a loyalty pledge, party leader Jarosław Kaczyński has announced. The dispute centres around a more moderate faction in the party aligned with former prime minister and deputy PiS leader Mateusz Morawiecki, who is one of those now set to be expelled from the party. They have for months been unhappy with PiS’s move in a hard-right direction. 💬 Prezes PiS Jarosław Kaczyński @OficjalnyJK. 👉 Udostępnij pic.twitter.com/bycjE0Yq0f — Prawo i Sprawiedliwość (@pisorgpl) July 24, 2026 “Around 30-something…of our group’s MPs have resigned,” revealed Kaczyński at a press conference on Friday. He added that their departures would be formalised at a meeting of the party’s political committee scheduled for Tuesday next week. Kaczyński’s announcement came after a deadline expired at midnight on Thursday for its MPs to sign a pledge of loyalty to the party that included a commitment not to be members of any external political associations. That measure was aimed in particular at an association called Development Plus (Rozwój Plus) founded by Morawiecki in April. The former prime minister had always insisted that his organisation was intended as complementary to PiS, rather than a rival to it. However, many figures in the party saw it as an attempt by Morawiecki to create a separate centre of power, and potentially to use the association as a launchpad for creating his own party ahead of the autumn 2027 parliamentary elections. The right-wing opposition PiS party has threatened disciplinary action, including exclusion from electoral lists, against dozens of its MPs who have joined a new internal group led by former PM @MorawieckiM and intended to appeal to more moderate voters https://t.co/y62Cm361U2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 17, 2026 After PiS issued a resolution on Wednesday last week requiring that its parliamentarians pledge to withdraw from any such associations, most of its 186 MPs quickly complied. However, a group of between 30 and 40 who are part of Development Plus refused to do so. “Everyone knew what they were supposed to sign, and knew the consequences of not signing,” said Kaczyński on Friday. “And so they made the decision they did.” “In this situation, we cannot view the [Development Plus] association as anything other than a component of a plan…to split our party,” he added. However, although its supporters will now leave PiS, “we want to part ways without any animosity”, said Kaczyński. After Kaczyński’s announcement, senior figures from Development Plus made clear that no one from their association had resigned from PiS. They had simply not signed the declaration of loyalty demanded by the party. Later, Morawiecki himself held a press conference in parliament surrounded by his supporters. He claimed that an unnamed “small group of schemers” within PiS had been seeking to turn Kaczyński against him and push him out of the party. “We fought for the unity of Law and Justice until the very end,” declared Morawiecki, who said that his group included 40 MPs, one senator and three MEPs. However, three of the MPs are not members of PiS, and therefore were not expected to sign the loyalty declaration. Szanowni Państwo! 🟦Do ostatniej chwili walczyłem o jedność Prawa i Sprawiedliwości. Nie o stanowiska. Nie o osobiste ambicje. Nie o wpływy. 🟦Walczyłem o jedność obozu, który przez osiem lat zmieniał Polskę – budował jej bezpieczeństwo, rozwijał gospodarkę i przywracał godność… pic.twitter.com/PP7sOkzMHp — Mateusz Morawiecki (@MorawieckiM) July 24, 2026 If the expulsion of Morawiecki’s supporters is confirmed, it will mark a major shake-up of Poland’s political landscape. PiS has for the last two decades been the dominant force on the Polish right, including periods leading governments in 2005-2007 and 2015-2023. However, since losing power at elections in 2023, when the party won 35% of the vote, PiS has seen its average support in polls fall to around 23-24%, the lowest level in 14 years. Meanwhile, it has been challenged by the rise of the far right, where two parties, Confederation (Konfederacja) and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), now together poll a similar combined level of support to PiS. In response, Kaczyński in March named a hardline figure, Przemyszław Czarnek, as PiS’s candidate for prime minister in next year’s elections. Czarnek was seen as someone who could appeal to far-right voters, while also potentially working with the far right if a coalition was needed after the elections. Support for PiS has fallen to its lowest in 14 years, as the party grapples with internal division, the rise of far-right challengers, living in President Nawrocki's shadow, and the unpopularity in Poland of PiS ally Donald Trump, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/QRScBpEQQG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 2, 2026 However, there has been no rise in support for PiS since Czarnek was named, prompting growing concern from more moderate figures within the party, led by Morawiecki. They argue that PiS has wrongly disowned many of the successes of its time in office before 2023, and they fear that its rightward shift damages its chances of winning over more centrist voters. Morawiecki, who was an international banker before joining PiS to become finance minister and then prime minister, wants the party to focus on more technocratic issues, such as economic development, rather than Euroscepticism and culture wars. That has led to frequent public sparring between his supporters and others in the party. In April, PiS threatened disciplinary action against members of Development Plus. Kaczyński and Morawiecki then reached an agreement that allowed the association to continue. But that uneasy truce has now fallen apart. World.title: Polish president renews bid for referendum on EU climate policy
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. President Karol Nawrocki has submitted a second request to parliament for a nationwide referendum on whether Poland should continue implementing the European Union’s climate policies, which he argues are too costly. Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, first proposed a referendum in May. But it was rejected by the Senate, the upper house of parliament, where the more liberal government has a majority. Senators argued that the proposed referendum question was “absurd”. The president has now submitted a revised proposal featuring a simplified question and again proposed holding the referendum on 27 September this year. Nawrocki’s originally proposed question was: “Are you in favour of implementing EU climate policy, which has led to an increase in citizens’ cost of living, energy prices and the cost of running business and agricultural activity?” However, following criticism in the Senate that the question was clearly intended to elicit a specific answer, this time he has proposed a more neutral one: “Are you in favour of Poland implementing the European Union’s climate policy?” “I’m looking for compromises, looking for solutions,” said Nawrocki on Thursday while announcing the new referendum bid. “The Senate wasn’t satisfied with the [previous] question”, so “we prepared a different one…[that] does not suggest anything”. However, the president has also proposed that the ballot paper would include information on what answering “yes” or “no” would mean in practice. Voters would be told, for example, that maintaining EU climate policy would result in, among other things, “Poland bearing costs estimated at 3.5 trillion zloty by 2040”, “burdens on agriculture”, “increasing costs for industry” and “obligations for owners of buildings”. By contrast, voting “no” would mean “negotiating exceptions and exemptions for Poland with the relevant EU bodies that will protect Polish industry and citizens from the burdens of climate policy”. Poland's right-wing opposition wants to withdraw from the EU Emissions Trading System, saying it makes Poles "a cash machine for absurd leftist climate policies"@PStrzalkowski explains what costs ETS really brings, and what prospects there are for reform https://t.co/UxpMWpG1pE — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 4, 2026 Under Poland’s constitution, the president may call a referendum with the approval of a majority of senators in a vote where at least half of all members of the 100-seat chamber are present. The ruling coalition of Prime Minister Donald Tusk controls 63 seats in the Senate, making approval of proposals brought forward by Nawrocki, who often clashes with the government and regularly vetoes its bills, unlikely. While the government is generally pro-EU, it has also been critical of Brussels’ green policies, arguing that they place too great a burden on Poland. After the European Commission last Friday unveiled changes intended to soften the impact of the Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS), the EU’s flagship climate policy, they were welcomed by the Polish government as a step in the right direction. Dzisiaj robimy milowy krok w zmianie systemu ETS. Po raz pierwszy Komisja Europejska proponuje rozwiązania, które łagodzą, a nie zaostrzają wpływ systemu na gospodarkę i obywateli. To efekt konsekwentnych działań Polski i zbudowania silnej koalicji państw w UE. Dzisiejsza… pic.twitter.com/5AMd9KCBVa — Ministerstwo Klimatu i Środowiska (@MKiS_GOV_PL) July 17, 2026 However, in his written justification for the new referendum proposal, Nawrocki wrote that, while he had “given the government time” in its push for ETS reform, the final result was simply “technical adjustments” that postpone some elements but do “not change the direction” or ultimate outcome. “ETS will remain an increasingly expensive, increasingly extensive system, and increasingly burdensome for the Polish economy,” wrote the president. The national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), which is the main opposition and supported Nawrocki’s bid for the presidency last year, wants Poland to unilaterally withdraw from ETS. Government figures warn, however, that there is no way to do so without either accruing enormous fines or leaving the EU entirely. When in power, PiS launched a revolution in Poland's energy transition. But now, in opposition, it has disowned those achievements and returned to an emphasis on coal. This could be a missed opportunity to win back centrist voters, writes @OrzelBartlomiej https://t.co/8cGvubn7N2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 29, 2026 Nawrocki’s new referendum proposal was met with criticism by figures from the ruling coalition. “There is no possibility of one country suspending part of EU law,” wrote Stanisław Gawłowski, a senator from Tusk’s Civic Coalition (KO) party. “This referendum is pure fraud.” Foreign minister Radosław Sikorski, also from KO, wrote that, “as the Brits have learned, the Europhobe’s dream world, in which one enjoys all the privileges of EU membership without any obligations, does not exist”. However, Nawrocki’s initiative was welcomed by Przemysław Czarnek, deputy leader of PiS, who wrote that, “on such fundamental matters as climate policy, Poles should decide, not Brussels bureaucrats”. Zaproponowane przez @NawrockiKn pytanie referendalne jest wybiórcze. Kontrpropozycja: „Czy jesteś za likwidacją unijnych dopłat do inwestycji i dla rolników?” Jak przekonali się Brytyjczycy, świat eurofoba, w którym ma się same przywileje członkostwa w UE, nie istnieje. — Radosław Sikorski 🇵🇱🇪🇺 (@sikorskiradek) July 23, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland appoints new human rights commissioner
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The government’s majority in parliament has chosen Sylwia Gregorczyk-Abram as Poland’s new human rights commissioner. She will take office after the five-year term of the incumbent, Marcin Wiącek, expires today. Gregorczyk-Abram is a prominent lawyer and activist, who is particularly well known for opposing the overhaul of the judiciary by the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. PiS, which is now the main opposition party, strongly opposed her election, arguing that she is politically aligned with the current, more liberal government. Gregorczyk-Abram herself, however, has pledged to “put all my beliefs and views aside” when she takes up the new role. Senat wyraził zgodę na powołanie Sylwii Gregorczyk-Abram na Rzecznika Praw Obywatelskich. pic.twitter.com/gz3rwGy3hi — Senat RP 🇵🇱 (@PolskiSenat) July 22, 2026 The commissioner for human rights (widely known by its Polish initials, RPO) is appointed by a resolution of the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, with the consent of the upper-house Senate. Candidates must meet certain requirements, including not belonging to any political party and having legal expertise and relevant experience. As well as acting as a watchdog for human rights, the RPO also has the power to submit motions to the Constitutional Tribunal to assess the constitutionality of laws and to file so-called cassation appeals to the Supreme Court and Supreme Administrative Court against rulings by lower courts. Poland’s human rights commissioner has written to the government expressing concern that a "temporary" ban on asylum claims by most migrants who irregularly cross the border from Belarus remains in place after more than a year https://t.co/9SA2TypQdK — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 28, 2026 Gregorczyk-Abram was last month nominated as a candidate to be the new RPO by the main ruling party, Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO), along with one of its coalition partners, The Left (Lewica). PiS proposed a rival candidate, Adam Borowski, a veteran of Poland’s anti-communist struggle in the 1980s. However, critics argued that Borowski, an activist and former PiS election candidate, does not appear to have the requisite legal knowledge and experience. In a Sejm vote last Friday, the ruling coalition supported Gregorczyk-Abram, who won 233 votes to Borowski’s 177. On Wednesday, her candidacy was also supported by the Senate, with 59 votes in favour and 25 against, confirming that she will become the new RPO. Gregorczyk-Abram is best known as one of the founders and leaders of the Free Courts (Wolne Sądy) initiative launched in 2017 amid a wave of protests against the then-PiS government’s efforts to take greater control over the judiciary. Free Courts was prominent in efforts to defend the rule of law. Many of its leading figures are now associated with the current ruling coalition: Maria Ejchart is a deputy justice minister, while Michał Wawrykiewicz is a member of the European Parliament representing KO. In April last year, Gregorczyk-Abram was made chairwoman of a commission established by the current government to look into cases of abuse of power against civil society under the former PiS administration. In September, her commission published its first findings, in which it said that public media outlets under PiS control had “carried out systematic repressive and defamatory actions against activists, non-governmental organisations, and civil society”. Poland's public media “carried out systematic repressive actions against activists, NGOs and civil society” during the rule of the former PiS government, a report commissioned by the new government has found https://t.co/S2MO9KGssC — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 26, 2025 PiS argues that Gregorczyk-Abram’s previous activity makes her unsuitable as a suitable candidate for RPO, which is meant to be a non-partisan role. They also point to claims that she was involved in a group of legal figures that discussed the Tusk government’s controversial takeover of public media in December 2023. “[She] is a discredited and extremely politicised person who should be brought to justice, and not receive the laurels of the commissioner for human rights,” former PiS justice minister Marcin Warchoł told the Do Rzeczy weekly last month. After a Sejm committee hearing on Gregorczyk-Abram’s candidacy earlier this month, former PiS deputy justice minister Sebastian Kaleta criticised her for ignoring questions over her alleged “role in the illegal takeover of public media”. Zadałem Sylwii Gregorczyk-Abram serię pytań o jej działania i możliwe spotkania z Ewą Wrzosek w sprawie przejęcia TVP, w tym możliwego tworzenia dokumentów prokuratorskich w prywatnej kancelarii. Kandydatka ostentacyjnie zdecydowała się ignorować te pytania. Ma bardzo dużo do… — Sebastian Kaleta (@sjkaleta) July 15, 2026 Speaking to state broadcaster TVP on Wednesday after her appointment was confirmed by the Senate, Gregorczyk-Abram declared that, “from the moment I take the oath and assume the position of commissioner, I will be independent and sovereign”. She pledged to “put all my beliefs and views – because each of us has them – aside and become an advocate for all citizens, regardless of what they believe in, how they live, or who they vote for”. Gregorczyk-Abram said that among her priorities as RPO would be the justice system, supporting the rights of disabled people and their carers, protecting older people, and fighting hate speech. With regard to the last of these issues, she noted that certain politicians present some groups as “enemies”, pointing to how this previously happened with LGBT+ people and judges, and is now being directed towards Ukrainians. Those are all groups who have at various stages been targeted by PiS and other right-wing parties. The number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland is up 30% so far this year, police data show. World.title: President to swear in new judge to Poland’s disputed constitutional court
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. President Karol Nawrocki has agreed to swear in a new judge to the Constitutional Tribunal (TK), ending weeks of doubt as to whether the opposition-aligned president would accept the judge appointed by the government’s parliamentary majority. Although Sławomir Patyra will now be accepted onto the court, four other judges appointed by parliament earlier this year continue to be excluded after Nawrocki refused to receive their oaths and the TK’s chief justice, also aligned with the opposition, blocked them from taking office. W najbliższy wtorek 28 lipca Prezydent Karol Nawrocki działając na postawie art. 4 ust. 1 ustawy o statusie sędziów Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, przyjmie ślubowanie od prof. Sławomira Patyry i tego samego dnia wręczy powołania czterem nowym sędziom Sądu Najwyższego. W przyszłym… — Zbigniew Bogucki🇵🇱 (@BoguckiZbigniew) July 22, 2026 Under Polish law, when a vacancy emerges among the 15 positions on the TK – for example when a judge’s nine-year term expires – the lower house of parliament, the Sejm, chooses who should fill it. However, to take office, the judge must swear an oath before the president. In April, after the Sejm had chosen six candidates to fill vacancies on the court, Nawrocki took the unprecedented step of inviting only two of them to be sworn in. He argued there were doubts over the legality of how all six had been chosen, but decided to accept two to ensure the TK had the necessary quorum to function. Those two have been able to take up their seats on the court, but the other four remain in limbo. Although they arranged their own private swearing-in ceremony without the presence of Nawrocki, the TK’s chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, has refused to accept them. In May, the European Court of Human Rights ordered that the quartet be allowed to take up their positions. But the TK – where judges appointed under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government retain a majority – issued its own ruling endorsing Nawrocki’s right not to swear in the new judges. On 11 June, the Sejm then chose another judge, Patyra, to fill a newly opened vacancy on the court. In his case, the legal doubts Nawrocki had expressed regarding the previous appointments, which in some instances were made more than a year after the vacancies had arisen, did not seem to apply. Yet for weeks the president refused to confirm whether he would swear him in. That prompted Patyra to write to Nawrocki in early July and then again this week, asking the president to indicate a date on which he could take his oath. Patyra himself has also made clear on which side of the dispute he stands. In an interview with news website Onet in May, he accused Nawrocki and Święczkowski of “blatantly unlawful actions” in deciding which TK judges can and cannot take office and suggested that the police should intervene. Sędzia TK prof. Patyra po raz kolejny zaapelował do Prezydenta o wyznaczenie mu terminu na złożenie przysięgi. Ignorowanie sędziego TK przez Prezydenta jest kolejnym przykładem psucia państwa. To pokazuje, jak bardzo siły anty-demokratyczne boją się odbudowy niezależnego TK.… — Dariusz Mazur (@_Dariusz_Mazur) July 21, 2026 Finally, on Wednesday this week, Nawrocki’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, announced that Nawrocki had invited Patyra to the presidential palace on Tuesday next week to take his oath. Speaking to Polsat News, Bogucki said that, in the case of Patyra, initially “there were some doubts, but the president dispelled them”, without specifying what they were. In the end, they concluded that “we had a fundamentally clean situation here” and Patyra was chosen “in accordance with all procedures”, unlike the six new judges chosen by the Sejm in March to fill longstanding vacancies. “It was not President Nawrocki or the current opposition who destroyed and are destroying the tribunal; it is the government that is doing it,” he added. The European Court of Human Rights has ordered Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) to accept four judges whom opposition-aligned President Nawrocki refused to swear in. The decision was welcomed by the government but rejected by the TK itself https://t.co/9NxInPdYk9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 6, 2026 The TK has been at the heart of the rule-of-law crisis that has developed in Poland over the last decade. In 2015, former PiS-aligned President Andrzej Duda refused to swear in three judges legally chosen by the Sejm. Shortly afterwards, PiS won parliamentary elections and nominated three replacements for those judges, who were sworn in by Duda. Those three judges and their successors have been deemed illegitimate in a succession of rulings by Polish and European courts. Due to their continued presence on the court, the current government, which replaced PiS in 2023, rejects the TK’s legitimacy and refuses to recognise its rulings. Under both Święczkowski, a former member of the PiS government, and his predecessor Julia Przyłębska, a close personal associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński, the TK has been widely seen as issuing rulings aligned with the political interests of PiS. We cannot do what we do without your support. Germany has deployed soldiers to Poland to help reinforce defences on NATO’s eastern flank in response to the threat of Russia. While Poland already hosts various allied forces, the presence of German troops is particularly symbolic given the two countries’ difficult history. “United, we will prevail,” wrote the General Staff of the Polish Armed Forces (SGWP), announcing the deployment. “This is what allied cooperation looks like in practice, which translates into greater military readiness and strengthens NATO’s defensive potential.” Polscy i niemieccy żołnierze razem wzmacniają granicę z Rosją. Takie rzeczy możliwe tylko za Tuska ☺️ pic.twitter.com/oNBME2gBsv — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) July 22, 2026 Last December, the Polish and German defence ministries revealed that a “mid-double-digit number” of German troops would be deployed from mid-2026 until the end of 2027 to support implementation of Poland’s East Shield operation, which seeks to bolster defences along the borders with Belarus and Russia. They said that the German personnel would mainly engage in engineering work, such as digging trenches, laying barbed wire and constructing anti-tank barriers. Today, Poland’s SGWP confirmed that “several dozen” German troops, including “highly specialised engineering forces” along with their equipment, had since June been temporarily deployed to “support the Polish armed forces in expanding defence infrastructure on NATO’s northeastern flank”. It emphasised that the East Shield project is “purely defensive in nature” and comes in “response to threats stemming from, among others, Russian aggression against Ukraine”. While the armed forces did not reveal the location of the deployment, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk indicated in a social media post that it was on the Russian border. Poland has a 210-km frontier with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. German public broadcaster Deutsche Welle reports that the activities of the German sappers are focused in particular on improving defences around the so-called Suwałki Gap, a strategically important stretch of land around the Polish-Lithuanian border between Belarus and Kaliningrad. “Together, we are ensuring Europe’s security,” said Lieutenant General Alexander Sollfrank, the Bundeswehr’s operational commander, announcing the deployment today. “Through our engagement in Poland, we are strengthening NATO’s defence capabilities and underscoring the alliance’s unwavering commitment to ensuring peace through unity and credible deterrence.” Poland and Germany have signed a bilateral security agreement that will see the two neighbours and NATO allies increase cooperation in areas such as military mobility, logistics infrastructure, maritime security in the Baltic Sea, and cybersecurity https://t.co/6BPX2WxvxH — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 17, 2026 SGWP, which shared footage of Polish and German forces installing anti-tank barriers, said the work aims to “hinder and delay an aggressor’s actions in the event of a threat”, thereby “increasing the time for a response from the Polish armed forces and the entire [NATO] alliance”. It also seeks to “create conditions for the efficient reception, deployment and use of NATO forces on Polish territory”. SGWP welcomed “the involvement of the German contingent as a practical expression of allied solidarity and the result of consistently developing military cooperation between Poland and Germany”. It also noted that the cooperation would help the two sides improve their ability to operate jointly, including “developing the competencies necessary for conducting a joint defence operation”. However, it emphasised that the current deployment is focused on training and engineering, with no combat component, and that the German troops are unarmed. SGWP also emphasised that the East Shield operation remains entirely a Polish national programme. The leaders of eight countries on the EU's eastern flank have met in the first summit of its kind to discuss closer security cooperation. The agreement is a sign that the two countries now stand “shoulder to shoulder, as equals”, declared German defence minister Boris Pistorius. Poland is also currently seeking a new permanent US military base on its territory, after President Donald Trump recently pledged to boost American troop numbers.
